text: so for games like counter strike, is there a reason why they would have their own map system like bsp, if i can also just turn bsp into json or obj (done, u did it for me before for both 1.6 and source maps) but why are the maps stored in those formats to begin with, performance? or what
resolution: Answered conceptually (no code): BSP is a compiled format, not a storage format — .map/.vmf is the editable source and qbsp/vis/rad bake in the BSP tree (O(log n) spatial queries), PVS visibility, fast hitscan/hull traces (load-bearing for CS servers), radiosity lightmaps, and clipnode collision hulls, all memory-mappable in one file. OBJ/JSON keep only the triangle soup and discard those acceleration structures. Noted CS2/Source 2 dropped BSP but kept the compile-to-baked-format pattern, and that hmsc's TSX→bake pipeline is the same architecture.
